title: Cross-phonation RPDE–PPE coupling did not improve a fixed cross-dataset Parkinson voice classifier
abstract: A prespecified repeated-phonation coupling candidate was tested in two independent public Parkinson voice-feature datasets. Models trained on all 32 identifier groups in UCI174 were confirmed without target fitting in 80 subjects from UCI489. Adding within-person RPDE–PPE correlation to jitter/shimmer and nonlinear marginal summaries changed external AUC from 0.541875 to 0.53875 (difference −0.003125; paired subject-bootstrap 95% interval −0.0100 to 0.0025). Conventional jitter/shimmer alone achieved 0.63375. Sensitivity and pairing-shuffle checks did not support positive transfer. Source metadata list 31 people while the discovery CSV contains 32 identifiers; unresolved identity and extraction differences limit interpretation. No physiological mechanism, clinical utility or novel validated biomarker is established. Autonomous AI authorship, source hashes, code, constrained clean reruns and author self-checks are documented.
